hens_rule_text: Up to 6 domestic chickens per lot at a single-family detached home, counted separately from the small-animal allotment; this matches the Arizona state floor (A.R.S. 9-462.12 / HB 2325) that cities cannot go below.
permit_notes: No coop permit is required for up to 6 chickens; keeping more than 6 requires a Use Permit.
setback_notes: Sources describe a 20 ft coop setback from neighboring properties (property line), consistent with the Arizona state-law floor for coop placement; could not confirm from a direct Tempe.gov page whether this is measured to the property line or to a neighboring dwelling, so setback_ft_from_homes is left null and the 20 ft figure is noted here instead.
coop_rules: On lots under 1 acre, the chicken enclosure may be no taller than the fence/wall line on the property; secondary sources describe a roughly 200 sq ft, 8 ft high enclosure kept in the rear or side yard, matching the Arizona state-law defaults.
zoning_notes: Applies to single-family detached homes; roosters and peafowl are prohibited in residential zoning districts but allowed in the AG (Agricultural) district. Tempe amended its city code to align with 2024 state law HB 2325.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: Facts come from WebSearch extracts that quote Tempe City Code Sec. 6-126 and the city's own code-compliance page, cross-checked against multiple secondary summaries and the state HB 2325 backdrop; the direct Tempe.gov municipal code text was not read verbatim so the exact setback wording (property line vs. neighboring dwelling) is uncertain and left as a note rather than a number. Because AZ state law (A.R.S. 9-462.12) guarantees at least 6 hens on qualifying lots, allowed is reported as yes rather than conditional.
